note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following diagnosis of ISUP grade group 4 prostate cancer.

The patient is a 62-year-old semi-retired musician living with his partner in a ground-floor apartment. He was diagnosed with prostate cancer following a biopsy in June 2024. His PSA has fluctuated, measuring 5.1 ng/mL in March 2022, 4.0 ng/mL in August 2023, and 6.4 ng/mL in February 2025. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 19/35. He has a history of inguinal hernial repair and is a former smoker with a 39 pack-year history, having quit in 2021. He consumes approximately 2 units of alcohol per week and leads a sedentary lifestyle with occasional walking. He recently attended routine appointments for a chest X-ray, podiatry, and thyroid screening.

On DRE, a suspicious nodule is palpable in the prostate, consistent with a clinical T stage of cT1c. General examination reveals a stable patient with normal vital signs. Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no palpable masses or lymphadenopathy.
